facts.subject: Ateshgah of Baku (Surakhani fire temple). Built 17th–18th c. (Wikipedia mirrors wikiwand/krisyotam/ipfs, wuf13.az, Atlas Obscura); UNESCO preslib: cells built between 17th–19th c. Used by Indian (mostly North Indian, Multan region) traders and pilgrims — Hindu, Sikh, Zoroastrian/Parsi worship (Wikipedia; UNESCO preslib: 'members of the Sikh community'). 24 cells for pilgrims (UNESCO preslib 'consist of 24 cells and rooms, which used to accommodate visiting pilgrims'; wuf13 '24 cells arranged in a pentagonal formation'). Inscriptions: 17 (Wikipedia: 14 Hindu, 2 Sikh, 1 Persian), 20 + 1 Persian (UNESCO preslib), 21 (wuf13), 'over 20' (Sify) -> wording 'təxminən 20'; languages Sanskrit (Devanagari), Punjabi (Gurmukhi), Persian. Natural flame went out in 1969 after heavy gas/oil extraction in the area (all sources); now fed by gas piped from Baku (wikiwand, krisyotam, Atlas Obscura, Better India). Museum 1975 (Wikipedia mirrors, Atlas Obscura); state historical-architectural reserve by decree 19 Dec 2007 (Wikipedia + UNESCO preslib). Ceased as a place of worship after 1883 (petroleum plants). NOT used: Dumas 1858 (one source), Alexander III 1888 (unverified), 'UNESCO World Heritage' (only Tentative List 1998), '500 years old' (Better India only), Zoroastrian-origin myths.

facts.subject: Leyla Mammadbeyova (Məmmədbəyova), born 17 Sep 1909 Baku, died 4 Jul 1989 (wikiwand/cavac Wikipedia text; preslib.az). First flight 1931 at the Baku airclub (wikiwand, cavac, azertag, azernews; preslib 'first flight in a U-1 aircraft'; Nargis: July 1931) -> aged 21. 'first female pilot of Transcaucasia, of Southern Europe and of Southwest Asia' (Wikipedia); 'first female pilot in Azerbaijan, the South Caucasus, and the Middle East' (preslib.az); Ogonyok mid-1930s 'Azerbaijani woman is the East's first woman pilot' (azertag). Parachute jump 17 Mar 1933, Moscow (Tushino per Wikipedia) — 'the second woman parachutist in the Soviet Union (after Nina Kamneva)' (Wikipedia); preslib: before her there were 84 Soviet paratroopers, only one a woman (azertag says 1934 — minority, 1933 used). Glider/parachute club trained about 4 000 paratroopers in the war (Wikipedia, preslib, Nargis). Six children (Wikipedia 'six overall', preslib 'a mother of six', Nargis); in the early 1930s already mother of two small children (azertag, azernews). Squadron leader 1941; last flight 1949. Buried in the Second Alley of Honour (preslib). NOT used: altitudes/'Soviet record' (not in sources), street/school names, 'first Muslim woman pilot' as a hard claim, medal years (preslib inconsistent), film titles.
